result.rationale: The diff shows `!booking.attendees.some((attendee) => guest === attendee.email)` in addGuests.handler.ts, a strict equality comparison. Email addresses are case-insensitive in practice, so 'Alice@Example.com' would bypass the duplicate check against an existing 'alice@example.com' attendee and be inserted via createMany, producing a duplicate attendee differing only in case. The mechanism is directly verifiable in the diff; whether case-differing duplicates actually occur in practice is the only soft spot, but the comparison is plainly case-sensitive.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `uniqueGuests` is computed with `!booking.attendees.some((attendee) => guest === attendee.email)` and `blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)`—both are case-sensitive string comparisons. Since the schema (`z.string().email()`) does not normalize casing, a guest like `Alice@Example.com` can bypass the “already attending” check if the stored attendee email is `alice@example.com`, resulting in duplicate attendees differing only by case.
